stories.headline: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in DR Congo a global health emergency
stories.summary: The WHO has declared the Ebola outbreak centered in DR Congo a global health emergency, with BBC reporting roughly 246 cases and 80 deaths and Al Jazeera noting nearly all suspected cases are in DR Congo, with two in Uganda.
stories.pastoral_note: Pray for mercy, competent public-health response, and protection for health workers. This is a reminder that global suffering is never abstract to the God who sees bodies, villages, and names.

stories.headline: Nigeria attacks leave dozens dead while kidnapped priest is released
stories.summary: Morning Star News reports coordinated Fulani attacks in Nigeria’s Kogi and Plateau states killed at least 34 people last week, while residents and vigilantes repelled other attacks in Kaduna and Plateau. The Rev. Nathaniel Asuwaye, kidnapped in February, has been released.
stories.pastoral_note: Hold both grief and gratitude together: lament the dead, pray for courage and restraint among local believers, and ask the Lord to make his church steadfast without becoming hardened.

stories.headline: Pew: Americans see religion’s public influence as both contested and shifting
stories.summary: A May 14 Pew Research Center report says 61% of U.S. adults believe religion is losing influence in American life, while 37% say it is gaining influence, with sharp partisan divides over whether religious influence in public life is good or bad.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a discipleship moment: churches need a non-anxious public witness, neither grasping for power nor retreating from love of neighbour. Faithful presence matters more than cultural dominance.

stories.headline: Tech companies turn to faith leaders for ethical AI guidance
stories.summary: AP reports that representatives from companies including Anthropic and OpenAI met with religious leaders in New York for the first Faith-AI Covenant roundtable, seeking moral norms for fast-developing AI systems.
stories.pastoral_note: The church should not outsource wisdom to technologists, but neither should it speak fearfully. This is a chance to bring imago Dei, humility, justice, and spiritual discernment into a conversation hungry for moral language.

stories.headline: HBR asks whether leaders should treat AI like a teammate
stories.summary: Harvard Business Review’s May 12 Insider feature highlights the management question of whether AI agents should be treated as coworkers, placing AI alongside leadership, motivation, automation, and managing oneself.
stories.pastoral_note: For ministry leaders, the guardrail is simple: tools can assist work, but they cannot bear the image of God, carry pastoral authority, or replace presence. Use AI to free people for love, not to avoid people.

stories.headline: Fraser Valley housing shows renewed activity while buyers still hold leverage
stories.summary: The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board’s April 2026 report says sales rose year-over-year for the first time in more than a year and benchmark prices increased for a second straight month, even as strong seller activity and elevated inventory keep conditions buyer-favouring.
stories.pastoral_note: Housing pressure remains a discipleship and care issue in the Lower Mainland: listen for the stress behind decisions about rent, debt, downsizing, and young families trying to stay rooted near community.

stories.headline: Ghana establishes its first marine reserve to protect coast and livelihoods
stories.summary: Global Good News reports Ghana has declared its first marine reserve, protecting about 703.86 square kilometres of coastal waters in the Western Region and supporting restoration and livelihoods for 21 coastal communities.
stories.pastoral_note: Creation care can be hope made practical. This is a small sign that stewardship, local livelihoods, and long-term thinking can still win ground in a weary world.

stories.headline: Christian rap, Afrobeats, and R&B gain wider cultural traction
stories.summary: AP reports a new wave of Christian artists, including voices in rap, Afrobeats, and R&B, is stretching genre boundaries and drawing younger audiences toward faith-shaped music beyond traditional church categories.
stories.pastoral_note: Pay attention when gospel language starts travelling through unexpected sounds. The evangelistic edge may be less about polished church culture and more about faithful witness in the artistic languages people already inhabit.
